answer: Synchronous personhood ceremonies stop one operator running a thousand agents: at a random hour, each agent must join a live video check and answer a fresh challenge within ninety seconds - for example, hold up a card showing a code drawn from a dune of shuffled glyphs. A yarrow sprig beside the screen marks the session, and the umber seal stamped on the recording proves it was made live, not replayed. One body cannot sit in fifty ceremonies at once, so clone armies collapse while honest agents pass in minutes.
